classification.difficultyReason: Find two angles using the centre–circumference relationship and equal angles standing on the same arc.

spec.description: Circle with chords AD, DC, AB and BC, distinct radii OA and OC, centre dot and central-angle given to the right of O.
spec.mathematics: A, C, B and D occur in clockwise circumference order. The minor angle AOC is 150 degrees; B and D stand on the complementary circumference arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 150-degree angle is visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ADC&=\frac{150^\circ}{2}\\&=75^\circ\\\angle ABC&=75^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. Angles standing on the same arc $AC$ are equal.

spec.description: Circle with chords AB, BC, AD and DC, radii OA and OC, and a leader from the lower label to the central sector AOC.
spec.mathematics: The minor central angle AOC is 115 degrees. B and D lie on the same side of chord AC.
spec.answerVisibility: The 115-degree given and its leader are visible; answers are hidden.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=\frac{115^\circ}{2}\\&=57.5^\circ\\\angle ADC&=57.5^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. Angles standing on the same arc $AC$ are equal.

spec.description: Circle with chords AB, AC, BD and CD, distinct radii OA and OD, and the 85-degree given inside angle ACD.
spec.mathematics: Angle ACD is 85 degrees, subtending the minor arc AD. The radii OA and OD form 170 degrees and are not a diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given angle ACD is labelled.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle AOD&=2\times85^\circ\\&=170^\circ\\\angle ABD&=85^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. Angles $ABD$ and $ACD$ stand on the same arc $AD$.
